Battle-damage exposed-frame build — a deliberate missing pauldron leaves a 9L Technic-beam rib and dark-grey cross-axle connector fully visible, a scorch-effect of dark-orange 1×1 cheese-slopes surrounds the gap, and a loosened ball-joint lets the arm hang at an off-angle, the war-torn salvage read entirely in brick geometry.

Shoulder-pauldron SNOT wing-plate stack — three overlapping dark-gunmetal wedge-4 slope-plates mounted on SNOT right-angle brackets off the shoulder-ball-joint housing, fanning outward in a layered wing-pauldron, each plate's smooth-tile face catching the light differently and the stagger creating depth no single flat build could achieve.

Trans-orange beam-blade weapon — a beam-sword hilt built from a 1×2 Technic-beam handle, clip-tile crossguard, and a 6L trans-orange lightsaber-bar blade socketed into a bar-holder, mounted on a clip-joint wrist so it angles forward in a guard-pose, the energy-blade read entirely from standard System and Technic elements.

Ankle-actuator piston greeble — a pneumatic-T-piece and short pneumatic-hose stub cross-pinned between the shin-beam and foot-plate bracket at each ankle, flanked by 2L axle-pins left exposed as hydraulic-line anchors, so the ankle joint reads as a powered actuator rather than a simple ratchet connection.

Chest-cavity greeble instrument-panel — behind the open cockpit-canopy a 4×4 back-wall of 1×1 round-tiles in dark-grey and light-bluish-grey, printed-tile warning-panels, and a trans-red 1×1 round-plate targeting-display form a dense instrument-cluster, the interior detail rewarding close inspection and anchoring the pilot's workspace in recognizable brick vocabulary.

CCBS-and-Technic hybrid torso shell — size-5 CCBS torso-shells snapped onto a central Technic-axle-and-beam spine, the organic CCBS curves meeting the angular Technic-beam edges at a visible seam that reads as deliberate design tension between biological and mechanical aesthetics, the constraction-system MOC hybrid at its most expressive.

Forearm missile-pod brick-build — a 2×4 stud-shooter cluster recessed into a forearm-housing of dark-gunmetal plate-tiles and 1×2 grille-tiles, the launcher-barrels protruding through a SNOT-plate fascia so they read as an integrated weapons-bay rather than an add-on accessory, the weapon architecture flush with the limb silhouette.

Liftarm rib-cage armor-gap detailing — 3L and 5L Technic-liftarms arranged as lateral ribs across the mech's abdomen with deliberate gaps between each, no armor-fill, so the negative space between the beams reads as ventilation-slats over the trans-cyan core beneath, the stripped-chassis aesthetic as a positive design choice.

Grille-tile shin-vent array — a vertical column of 1×2 grille-tiles inset flush into a 2×8 plate-channel on each shin-plate, framed by 1×1 cheese-slope corners, the parallel grille-fins implying internal cooling-fins channeling waste heat from the knee-actuators, the surface-read of working machinery in four tiles of brick.

Hip-rotation Technic-turntable integration — a Technic large-turntable ring at the waist-join allows the upper torso to rotate independently of the leg-assembly, the ring's exposed gear-teeth left visible between the hip-armor plates as a deliberate mechanical-detail rather than concealed, the moving joint read as kinetic engineering.

Trans-blue light-pipe shoulder-conduit — a 4L bar-element in trans-blue routed through a drilled-channel gap in the pauldron-plates from the chest-core outward, exiting as a glowing stub at the shoulder-seam, the light-pipe implying powered energy-routing through the armor structure as a visual narrative told entirely in transparent brick elements.

Clawed splay-foot ball-joint build — each mech-foot built from a Bionicle foot-plate base with three Bionicle-claw elements on 1L clip-joints fanned outward and a heel-spur of a 2L Technic-axle-pin, the ball-joint ankle above allowing the splayed foot to flatten fully against any display surface for a stable ground-contact.

Weapon-arm beam-cannon barrel greeble — a 3×3 round-brick housing wraps the cannon-barrel mid-point, flanked by 1×1 round-plate cooling-rings in dark-gunmetal and a trans-cyan 1×1 round-plate muzzle-charge indicator, the barrel-assembly reading as a charged energy-weapon ready to fire through stacked round-geometry alone, no sticker or print required.

Hydraulic-piston greeble at knee-joint — Technic pneumatic-T-bar cylinders paired with 3L Technic pins bracket the knee on both sides, reading as pressurized actuators firing into the joint-housing with dense mechanical greeble weight.

Panel-line + vent detailing on pauldrons — shoulder-armor broken up with inset rows of 1×2 grille-tiles, 1×1 cheese-slopes at panel corners, and exposed Technic pin-stubs, layering convention-grade surface density across the flat pauldron faces.

Reverse-joint digitigrade bird-leg — the scout-mech's lower leg built with ratchet-click-hinge bricks bent backward at the ankle, terminating in a claw-foot of three 3L Technic fingers splay-pinned into a gripping ground-contact stance.

Battle-damage armor-gap — a deliberately missing pauldron-panel exposes the 11L Technic liftarm shoulder-frame and a flickering dark-trans-orange 1×1 round-plate scorch-tile, with the ball-joint socket left bare as a punctured-armor combat-read.

Layered SNOT hip-armor skirt — overlapping 2×3 slope-tiles and 1×2 jumper-plates mounted on sideways SNOT hinge-plates around the hip-ring build a layered skirt of angled panels that flex with the ball-joint pelvis without binding.

Light-piping limb routing — trans-blue 3L bar-elements threaded through gaps between CCBS shell segments carry the power-core glow from the torso reactor into the forearm-vents, the light-piping technique making energy-flow legible in solid brick geometry.

Greebled instrument-panel in cockpit — the pilot minifig's console built from a 4×6 plate base studded with 1×1 round-tiles, 1×1 cheese-slopes, and a 1×2 grille-tile radar-screen, compressing believable instrument-density into minifig-scale brick architecture.

Shoulder-ratchet firing pose — both arms locked into a wide-armed targeting stance via click-hinge ratchet-joints at the shoulder-to-torso connection, the defined click-positions holding the weight of the cannon-arm assembly without drift.

Trans-cyan knee-reactor node — a secondary power-node at the knee built from a trans-cyan 2×2 dome-brick set into a ring of dark-bluish-gray 1×1 plate-with-ring surrounds, glowing outward through the hydraulic-piston greeble gap.

Technic-pin vent array on shin — the shin-armor plate punctuated by a grid of exposed Technic cross-axle pins pushed through a 4×6 panel-brick, reading as active cooling-vents with the pin-heads flush to the armor surface.

CCBS shoulder-armor ball-mount — a Bionicle CCBS large shell clipped directly onto the Technic ball-joint at the shoulder-socket, letting the shell rotate and tilt with the arm-pose while presenting a smooth convex pauldron face forward.

Stacked wedge-slope chest-V — the mech's chest V-shaped sternum built from mirrored 4×2 inverted-wedge-slopes mounted on SNOT brackets, their angled faces forming an aggressive forward-pointing chest-profile with a clean center-seam panel-line.

Missile-pod brick-build forearm — the left forearm houses three side-by-side 1×1 round-bricks capped with trans-red 1×1 round-tiles as warhead-noses, set into a 2×6 plate housing clipped to the CCBS forearm-bone as a loaded pod-mount.

Battle-damaged bent limb — the left leg's knee ratchet-joint deliberately loosened two clicks below neutral and the shin CCBS shell removed, the exposed 3L Technic bone + axle-connector gap reading as a combat-damaged joint still bearing weight.

Turntable waist-pivot articulation — a 4×4 Technic turntable-brick at the mech's waist lets the upper torso rotate independently of the hip-assembly, the twist posed mid-action so the cannon-arm tracks left while the legs plant right.

Hydraulic-shoulder actuator pair — two Technic pneumatic-cylinder assemblies mounted diagonally across the upper-back between the shoulder-liftarms and spine-beam, reading as powered actuators driving the arms with the cylinder-rods extended into the joint-housing greeble.

COCKPIT REVEAL — the mech's upper-torso hinged open on a 2×2 Technic turntable to expose a trans-clear curved canopy brick sheltering a seated pilot minifig at a dash of 1×1 round-tiles and clip-mounted lever controls, the human-scale anchor inside the titan.
